Ooh that's an interesting one. To be honest I've never bought a used game that didn't come with original packaging. It's just that the places I buy them from don't deal in games without them. So much yes to this question. I may as well buy a game digitally (steam, psn, nintendo store) if I weren't going to get a fully boxed game.

The paper/plastic aren't worth very much in material cost? True, but in collectible cost, they are seriously worth getting. If a game is just mildly good, then sure if the physical copy is cheaper than digital, I'll buy it from a used game store sans packaging. But if it's a game I think is worth playing, or has a good market value, I'm snatching that up in good condition. Digital media is overrated, useful and should still exist, yes, but overrated.

Why do I like physical media? No practical reasons. Simply because I love having something I can look at, put on a shelf and feel. This applies to books, music, comics/manga, anime/cartoons and live action stuff. I am not simply a consumer of media, I am a collector. That's how I like to think of my interaction with this, at least.

EDIT: Misleading references to used games. I love used games so long as they are boxed and in good condition.
